contract: One MCP server over Streamable HTTP through ex_mcp 1.8.1: inert, bounded, untrusted tool discovery that never calls a tool; one tools/call per dispatch identity, admitted from a core/effect declaration carrying a caller-supplied exact-action release reference and bound to the delivery/effect-intent owner: completed{content, is_error, structured}; refused{unknown_tool | invalid_arguments | too_large | credentials_unavailable | not_connected | target_refused | invalid_request} decided locally before sending, or refused{authentication_failed} for an HTTP 401/403 (named upstream assumption, dispatched); unknown{reason} for any timeout, broken connection, input-required result or JSON-RPC error after sending. No resend: fail-closed auth provider, reconnect and health ping off, no standalone GET stream, per-operation retry_policy false, http_stream_retry :safe_only and max_mrtr_rounds 0; no client handler; injected credential Need; allowlisted endpoint under a loopback, private or public network policy.
limits: ExMCP.Client.make_request/5 is @doc false at ex_mcp 1.8.1 (pinned exactly): an upstream risk guarded by drift tests; ExMCP.Client.call_tool/4 is not used because it resends tools/call after a -32020 header-mismatch error.

A tool result's content is delivered to the recipient Need by best-effort in-memory mailbox delivery only; the intent store keeps a sealed digest. A recipient that has exited loses the content; the settlement is unchanged.
The discovery snapshot is a local, possibly stale admission filter; it claims nothing about the server's current tool set or schema.
One transport (Streamable HTTP); no stdio, OAuth, resources, prompts, subscriptions, tasks or sampling; no claim about what a tool does on its server.
ex_mcp's own [:ex_mcp, ...] telemetry and debug logs are emitted upstream and reach consumer handlers; no credential was observed in them in the tested scenarios only.
Finite tests against an in-process loopback server (ex_mcp's own server behind a recording Plug); no TLS or public endpoint in the evidence; no proof is claimed.

grounding.claim: Pinned Cure compilation type-checks the pure stage/reply-to-outcome decision used at runtime; not a proof of transport behaviour.

Named scenarios against an in-process loopback MCP server: connect handshake per protocol mode, bounded discovery, completed and tool-error results, snapshot refusals, release reference, too large, 401/403 with one tools/call and no OAuth, timeout, killed connection, broken stream drift control, 503, JSON-RPC errors including -32020 with one tools/call, input_required, malformed and oversize responses, no reconnect or ping, duplicate dispatch, server-initiated requests, credential Need failures, redaction, best-effort delivery, close, configuration, forged completion, classification table, interop and the exact pin; finite evidence, not proof.

ex_mcp 1.8.1 client, era negotiation and Streamable HTTP transport as read at the pinned version: per-operation retry options, MRTR round limit, auth-provider challenge handling, delivery_outcome/1's :not_sent classification and the @doc false make_request/5; MCP 2025-11-25 and 2026-07-28 semantics are named, not proved.

An HTTP 401 or 403 authentication rejection means the server did not execute the call (never an attested no-send); ex_mcp's :not_sent attestation is true for the reasons it lists (tested scenarios only); the host keeps the credential Need, the endpoint allowlist and the recipient Need truthful.

telemetry.contract: No events of its own. ex_mcp emits upstream [:ex_mcp, ...] events that consumer-installed handlers may see (the consumer's responsibility). Own events through runtime/telemetry: future task when a consumer needs them. Not inherited: runtime/telemetry is not a dependency of this Piece.

config.contract: Build-time binding (server identity, allowlisted endpoint, network policy, id, recovery grace) entering the intent key; construction-time protocol mode, timeouts, request/response/discovery bounds and credential Need; per-request deadline from the declaration; no hot update.

control.contract: close/1 ends the connection and in-flight calls end unknown; no pause or drain. Dispatch, rearm, poll and expiry are the delivery/effect-intent owner's Control.
